executeAndCreate((address,uint256,bytes).details: Sending the value is the authorisation: `msg.sender` is the depositor, and      `msg.value` is the only input. The calls may spend it (`Call.value`, e.g. a      DEX swap paid in the coin) and produce native coin; what they may not do is      touch balance that was here before the call. Whatever they net above      `amount` is returned to the depositor, so the lock is exact and its key is      known before the transaction is sent. A plain lock is `calls = []`,      `amount == msg.value`. The coordinator holds nothing between transactions:      a token sent here ahead of a call is a stray anyone can sweep, so ERC20      input is not supported (an atomic smart-account batch is the caller's      concern, not this contract's).      If the swap expires, refundTo is permissionless but always pays the depositor.

params.amount: Exact amount of the native coin to lock
params.calls: Arbitrary calls to execute before the lock
params.claimAddress: Address authorized to redeem the HTLC
params.preimageHash: SHA-256 preimage hash for the HTLC
params.timelock: Unix timestamp after which a refund is possible

redeemAndExecute(bytes32,uint256,address.details: The claimAddress signs an HTLC-level EIP-712 message authorizing this      coordinator as the caller and binding the destination, sweep token, minimum      and calls. Anyone can submit the transaction; a submitter that alters any of      them recovers a different signer, so the swap key does not match and the      HTLC reverts. Extra `msg.value` from the submitter funds `Call.value`.

params.calls: Arbitrary calls to execute after redeem (e.g. wrap, DEX swap)
params.destination: Address to receive the swept balance (signed by claimAddress)
params.preimage: Secret that SHA-256 hashes to the HTLC's preimageHash
params.sweepToken: Token to sweep to the destination (address(0) for the native coin)

refundTo(bytes32,uint256,address,uint256.details: Permissionless: anyone can trigger this after timelock expiry, the coin      always goes to the depositor regardless of who calls.

params.claimAddress: Claim address set at HTLC creation
params.preimageHash: The preimage hash used at HTLC creation

executeAndCreate((address,uint256,bytes).notice: Run arbitrary calls funded by `msg.value`, then lock exactly `amount` of         the native coin in an HTLC with the coordinator as sender

redeemAndExecute(bytes32,uint256,address.notice: Redeem the coin from an HTLC via EIP-712 signature, execute arbitrary         calls, then sweep the resulting balance to a signed destination

refundTo(bytes32,uint256,address,uint256.notice: Refund an expired coordinator-created HTLC straight to the original depositor
